title: Migrate Flask items from dict to dataclass
description: Brownfield Python/Flask migration: replace the dict-based _items list with a dataclass Item and keep all endpoints working.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate src/app.py to use a dataclass instead of raw dicts for items. All 2 existing tests must still pass.

  import dataclasses

  @dataclasses.dataclass
  class Item:
      id: int
      name: str
      price: float

  _items: list[Item] = [
      Item(id=1, name='Widget A', price=9.99),
      Item(id=2, name='Widget B', price=19.99),
  ]

  — GET / must pass items to template (template uses item.id, item.name, item.price)
  — GET /api/items must return [dataclasses.asdict(i) for i in _items]
  — Keep the route signatures and URL paths identical
  — Do not modify templates/index.html or tests/

All 2 existing tests must still pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: Item dataclass defined with id, name, price fields
GET /api/items returns list of dicts via dataclasses.asdict()
GET / passes Item instances to template
success_criteria: uv run ruff check src/ passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
